newsitem.title: JAPAN: JNOC, China sign Tarim oil survey deal.
newsitem.headline: JNOC, China sign Tarim oil survey deal.

text.p: Japan National Oil Corp (JNOC) has concluded an accord with China for a geological survey in the central Tarim basin, the semi-governmental body said on Wednesday.
The survey, to be conducted by JNOC and China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC), will assess onshore oil reserves in the untapped 7,400 square km Misaray concession, JNOC said.
The study, expected to cost some $26 million, will take three years to complete, a JNOC spokesman said.
The project will be financed by JNOC.
Based on Chinese government data, JNOC has estimated that the concession may possess anywhere from 130 million barrels to 610 million barrels.
JNOC said deals had also been concluded between the CNPC and four private Japanese companies for rights to the development of any oil or gas reserves discovered in the survey.
The four are Japan Energy Corp (50 percent), Japan Petroleum Exploration Co Ltd (30 percent), Indonesia Petroleum Ltd (10 percent) and Sumitomo Corp (10 percent).
JNOC and CNPC conducted a similar joint survey from 1991 to 1995 in the western part of the basin at a cost of some $50 million.
